title: Jalapeño-Popper Smash Burgers with Raspberry-Bacon Jam
summary: Double jalapeño smash burgers with Havarti, whipped cream cheese and a bacon jam made with coffee, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar and fresh raspberries. burgerfection recreates and reviews Alf's Kitchen's recipe; most quantities and the patty cooking times are not supplied.

steps.text: Cook the diced bacon over medium-high heat. Remove the cooked bacon and let it drain.
Discard the bacon grease from the pan, then add the white onion.
Add the black coffee, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar and fresh raspberries.
Add salt and pepper and return the bacon to the pan.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 45–50 minutes, until the mixture becomes bacon jam. The creator shows it ready after about 45 minutes.

ingredients.amount: 2–3 oz per patty; 2 patties per burger
ingredients.note: The 75/25 blend is specified at 0:47. The reviewer gives the 2–3 oz patty weight at 2:01; the two-patty assembly is stated at 1:18. Total batch size is not stated.
Named at 1:04; the automatic captions render it as 'havari'. The creator says he normally uses American cheese but chooses Havarti for this version.

steps.text: Use 75/25 ground beef for the smash burgers. The reviewer describes the patties as 2–3 oz each later in the video.
Place the thinly sliced jalapeños on top of the patties before smashing them down. Put any fallen jalapeño slices back on top afterward.
Top the patties with Havarti. Once the cheese has melted, take the burgers off the cooking surface. The narration does not specify a flip point or cooking time.

ingredients.note: Assembly names one bottom bun and one top bun; no total batch yield is given.

steps.text: Spread a generous amount of whipped cream cheese on the bottom bun.
Place two jalapeño patties on the cream cheese.
Spread a good amount of the raspberry-bacon jam on the top bun, then close the burger.

notes: This upload is burgerfection's recreation and review of a recipe credited in the video to Alf's Kitchen, not an upload from Alf's Kitchen's own account.
The jam spread is described as 'a good amount' at 1:23; no measured jam quantity or jam yield is supplied.

At 2:23 the reviewer suggests dry-toasting the bun. At 2:40 he suggests replacing the coffee with Scotch or bourbon. These are review suggestions, not ingredients or steps in the demonstrated version above.
